title: Pictures on the whole page: lighter files, a lighter format, or baked end-screen backgrounds (3 options)
problem:
The end-screen backgrounds cause most of the slow frames after you lift the finger (phone test: 16 per run with them, 3 without).
- Your blind swipe agreed.
- The page downloads 89 picture files (10.4 MB) on a phone; 21 of them (3.3 MB) are never drawn there.
- 27 pictures are bigger than a phone screen can show; 10 photos are stored as PNG, a heavy format for photos.
- The end screen redraws grain mixed in with a blend effect, and a live-blurred photo, on every toolbar step.

options.name: lighter-files
options.label: A: lighter files
options.idea:
Shrink 22 oversized pictures to exactly what a phone shows, same file type.
- 3 phone pixels per page pixel, so nothing gets blurry on the iPhone.
- The menu photo wall loads pictures only when shown: the 8 photos a phone hides are never downloaded.
- 5 more were left as they are: their shrunk file came out bigger than the original.
options.looksSame: Nearly: a shrunk photo can look a touch softer. In the Chrome check only a few small pictures changed (largest 0.06 % of the screen).
options.risk:
Lag effect not measured yet; the phone test after you pick decides.
- This test build swaps the files for every screen size; a real change would add phone sizes (srcset), so computers keep today's files.
- The hero intro could not be compared by screenshot: it differs between two loads of the same page.
visualDiff: A few avatars and seller photos, slightly softer at most; nothing moves.

gain.how: Chrome, 430 px wide at 3x, one load and one full scroll per build.
Chrome trace; the draws come from repaints, not from file size.

shots.caption: Commission section avatars, the biggest change in the Chrome check (430 px, 3x)

options.name: new-format
options.label: B: A plus AVIF
options.idea:
Everything in A, plus 32 pictures re-saved as AVIF.
- AVIF is a modern photo format Safari reads since iOS 16 (webkit.org, Safari 16.0 notes).
- The page links to the new files.
options.looksSame: Nearly: AVIF changes pixels slightly. In the Chrome check the largest change outside the hero intro was a small avatar row (0.07 % of the screen).
options.risk:
Same as A.
- AVIF takes a little more phone work to unpack the first time a picture appears; not measured on the phone yet.
- 3 seller photos whose links are built while the page runs keep their old format (shrunk only).
visualDiff: As A, plus faint compression changes in photos; nothing moves.

gain.how: Chrome, 430 px wide at 3x, one load and one full scroll per build.

options.name: baked-backgrounds
options.label: C: baked end-screen backgrounds
options.idea:
On phones the 4 end-screen background boxes show one still picture each, made from today's page.
- Grain with its blend effect, soft gradient and blurred photo are drawn once into the picture, not live on every redraw.
- Everything on top of them stays live; up to 640 px wide only.
options.looksSame:
Nearly: only inside the 4 boxes.
- Most pixels change by up to 20 of 255 shades (compression of the saved picture on the grain).
- One spot has about 4,000 pixels that change more.
options.risk:
Chrome cannot show the gain; the phone test after you pick decides.
- It may not remove the whole lag: the phone test also hid the animated colour titles at the end, and they redraw about 100 times per scroll. We are measuring that part separately now.
- Adds about 1 MB of download.
- On phones narrower than 430 px the grain is scaled slightly. Computers are unchanged.
visualDiff: The grain dots in the 4 end-screen boxes can sit in slightly different places; colours, sizes and positions are the same.

gain.what: Live blend or blur layers at the end
gain.how: 2 stage grain blends, the invoice sheet's grain blend and mesh photo, 1 blurred stage photo. The agents panel's grain stays.
Chrome, one load and one full scroll.
One run each; today's build varied 1306-1324 in 3 runs. Chrome blends on its GPU, so it cannot show this option's gain.

shots.caption: Two end-screen boxes: live grain and gradient (A) vs baked picture (B), 430 px, 3x
The blurred-photo box and the invoice sheet (430 px, 3x)

recommended.why:
C is the only option aimed at the slow frames.
- It removes the live blend and blur work the phone test pointed at; A and B save download and memory, not redraw work.
- After you pick, a phone test measures the slow frames; A or B can be added on top.

revisions.note: Option A corrected: 5 pictures whose shrunk file came out bigger stay as they are; A now saves 3.8 MB (was shown as 3.0). Option C notes that the animated colour titles may carry part of the lag; measured separately next.
